questions.q: Why is `operator+` in the Money example implemented by calling `operator+=` rather than duplicating the addition logic?
options: operator+= is required by the C++ standard before operator+ can be defined
It avoids duplicating the same logic in two places and keeps a single source of truth for addition
operator+ cannot access private members otherwise
It makes the function run in constant time
questions.explain: Building the free operator+ on top of the member operator+= is a common idiom that avoids repeating the same mutation logic twice.

questions.q: Why must `operator<<` for printing a custom type to std::ostream be a free (non-member) function?
options: Member functions cannot be marked friend
ostream objects cannot be passed by reference
The left-hand operand of << is std::ostream, a type you don't own, so you cannot add a member function to it
Free functions execute faster than member functions
questions.explain: A member function is invoked as leftOperand.function(), so << would need to be a member of ostream itself — which you cannot modify. It must be a free function instead.

questions.q: What does marking `operator<=>` as `= default` do in C++20?
options: It deletes the comparison operator
It generates the comparison by comparing each member in declaration order automatically
It makes the operator return true unconditionally
It requires the programmer to still write the comparison logic by hand
questions.explain: A defaulted spaceship operator performs member-wise comparison in declaration order, and can also generate <, <=, >, and >= from that single definition.

questions.q: Which scenario is a good candidate for operator overloading, per the lesson's guidance?
options: Overloading + on a Position type to mean 'cancel this position'
Overloading == on a Money type to compare the underlying cent values for equality
Overloading * on a Trade type to mean 'send an email notification'
Overloading << on an Order type to mean 'submit the order to the exchange'
questions.explain: Operators should be overloaded only when their meaning matches programmer intuition — == for value equality is intuitive; using + or << for unrelated actions is not.

questions.q: Why does the free `operator+(Money lhs, const Money& rhs)` take its first parameter by value instead of by reference?
options: By-value parameters cannot be modified inside the function
It gives the function a local copy it can safely mutate (via +=) and return, without altering the caller's original object
C++ forbids reference parameters in free functions
It is required for the function to be a friend
questions.explain: Taking the left operand by value creates a copy that operator+ can mutate with += and then return, leaving the caller's original Money object untouched.
